_provenance.purpose: Hand-curated editorial layer for the /waterways/buckingham-canal page. Every fact carries source, date and flag (verified | inferred | asserted). Derived exclusively from docs/research/buckingham-canal/ (dossier.md, sections 01-07, data-vintages.md). Banned claims list enforced by scripts/verify_waterway_buckingham.py.

sea mouths serve this stretch; the Cooum, Adyar and Muttukadu mouths close with sand for much of the year; the Ennore mouth stays open but keeps filling with sand

reaches.name: Ennore Creek crossing
reaches.verdict: The canal crosses the Kosasthalaiyar mouth zone on the same level, through a creek complex silted a metre deep with fly ash.

facts.text: Fly-ash silting about 1 m deep on the 2.5 km NCTPS-Kamarajar stretch; WRD dredging of ~4.30 lakh cubic metres began mid-2020 under NGT direction, funded by a Rs 28.5 crore Tangedco deposit plus Rs 66.23 lakh for the North Buckingham Canal.
facts.source: The Hindu via ICSF; NGT record

facts.text: A mass fish kill hit this reach 15-17 Aug 2026 (~6-7 km, Kattukuppam to Kolivakkam): tonnes of mullet, ladyfish, croakers, prawns and crabs. Fishers blocked the Ennore expressway. TNPCB lab results were pending as of 18 Aug 2026.
facts.source: The South First; The Federal; Deccan Chronicle

facts.text: A citizen field study measured water at 40.8 C in the canal near the Railway Bridge, 585 m from NTECL Vallur's discharge point, on 9 Aug 2026, and attributes the kill to hot-water and chemical discharge. This attribution is the campaign's, not TNPCB's.
facts.source: Save Ennore Creek Campaign press release

facts.text: The invasive charru mussel (Mytella strigata) has spread across the Kosasthalaiyar backwater and the canal; NCSCM found it at ~24% of 197 sampling points at densities above 800 per sq m. WRD sought Rs 160 crore from Kamarajar Port for removal.

reaches.name: Athipattu to ETPS
reaches.verdict: The power-station reach: the road bridge here is literally named the Flyash Bridge.

facts.text: Ash slurry pipelines cross the canal en route to the NCTPS ash pond; reporting found spots where canal flow is completely dead nearest the plant, with low tide exposing thick ash-silt deposits.
facts.source: The News Minute; India Water Portal

facts.text: On current consents, NCTPS Stages I and II are permitted to discharge 2.38 and 4.90 million KLD of cooling water respectively into the Ennore creek system - the largest consented discharges there.

reaches.name: ETPS to Manali refinery belt
reaches.verdict: Consents have moved routine industrial discharge off this reach; the watch now is storm-season events and the municipal load.

facts.text: On TNPCB's consent books (latest orders 2021-2026), no Manali process industry may discharge effluent to the canal: CPCL is reuse-only (with a consented monsoon stormwater route to the canal, monitored by online sensors and booms), Indian Additives and Ashok Leyland are zero-liquid-discharge, TPL discharges to sea.
facts.source: 13 TNPCB OCMMS consent orders, pulled 18 Aug 2026

facts.text: TNPCB's Manali CEPI action plan states there is 'no disposal of treated trade effluent/sewage into Buckingham canal', attributing the canal's load to 7.8 MLD of untreated municipal sewage from local bodies without underground sewerage.
facts.source: TNPCB CEPI action plan for Manali

facts.text: During Cyclone Michaung flooding on 4 Dec 2023, an estimated 24,000 litres of CPCL crude entered the Buckingham Canal and spread through it to the creek and sea, affecting ~20 sq km and ~9 fishing villages; relief of Rs 8.68 crore went to 9,001 affected families, including Rs 12,500 each to 2,301 fishing families and Rs 10,000 per boat for 787 boats.

Ashok Leyland's Ennore consent expired on 31 Mar 2026 with no renewal visible in the public OCMMS search as of 20 Aug 2026 (it may sit in TNPCB's non-public auto-renewal scheme); a March 2026 order for the co-located Ashok Leyland Defence Systems, valid to 31 March 2030, records trade effluent NIL and sewage to land.

reaches.name: Manali to Kodungaiyur
reaches.verdict: Where the city's sewerage system meets the canal: three treatment outfalls, and the pumping stations the next round of interception is set to relieve.

facts.text: The Kodungaiyur STP cluster's 40, 80 and 110 MLD outlets discharge to this reach; TNPCB files them under 'Buckingham Canal River'. In 2022-23 the 80 MLD outlet hit BOD 51 mg/L against a 10 mg/L norm.
Six CMWSSB pumping stations in Tiruvottiyur discharge at least 7.25 MLD of raw sewage directly into the canal, per CMWSSB's own RTI replies reproduced in a citizens' audit.
Median measured water width on this reach: 25 m.
Tondiarpet, Old Washermanpet, Korukkupet and Mint, alongside the canal, are the city's worst Culex mosquito clusters; the canal is GCC's named top breeding source.
facts.source: Madras Musings; Citizen Matters (GCC vector control)

reaches.name: Korukkupet to Basin Bridge
reaches.verdict: Two of the city's dirtiest drains, the Otteri Nullah and Captain Cotton Canal, join here at Basin Bridge.

facts.text: Otteri Nullah (38.4 sq km catchment) and the Captain Cotton Canal join the Buckingham Canal at Basin Bridge.
facts.source: IIT Madras rapid assessment of the 2015 flood

facts.text: CPCB's Captain Cotton Canal station recorded dissolved oxygen as low as 0.3 mg/L and BOD up to 120 mg/L in 2024.

reaches.name: Basin Bridge to the Cooum junction
reaches.verdict: The canal squeezes past Chennai Central and meets the Cooum; the first MRTS crossing appears.

facts.text: The North Canal joins the Cooum's north bank at the same level behind Chennai Central; there is no continuous canal channel through the junction.

reaches.name: The Cooum link
reaches.verdict: For 1.3 km the through-route is the tidal Cooum river itself; the South Canal takes off 150 m west of Napier Bridge.

facts.text: TNPCB sampling reported in Feb 2025 found the canal's salinity maxima near Napier Bridge (TDS 5,560 mg/L; chloride and sulphate together 2,599 mg/L): the tidal signature of the Cooum mouth.

The South Buckingham Canal is a tidal canal taking off from the Cooum and running 110 km to Kovalam North lock near Marakkanam, with seven sea openings, lock-controlled, whose sand bars keep them closed about seven months a year.

reaches.name: Triplicane to Ice House
reaches.verdict: The narrowest water in the city: 9 m at the minimum where the survey records say 42 to 143 m.

facts.text: Measured water width on this reach: median 18 m, minimum 9.3 m.
IWAI's condition survey found the city stretch 'totally in abandoned condition', width 10-15 m, with MRTS columns standing in the canal bed itself.
Original survey widths between the Cooum and Adyar ran 42 m (Wallajah Road) to 143 m (St Mary's Road); current widths 24-48 m.
facts.source: HSCTC feasibility report (~2012), via Wikipedia (table added 25 Aug 2013)

facts.text: CPCB's Ice House station recorded DO pinned at 0.3 mg/L through all of 2024, with BOD up to 141 mg/L - the worst year in the five-edition record.
TNPCB's Wallajah Road station logged monthly BOD between 9 (December, monsoon flush) and 150 mg/L (April) in 2022-23. The monitoring series ends there: no CCWW edition has been published since.
facts.source: TNPCB CCWW 2022-23; TNPCB waterquality page checked 18 Aug 2026

reaches.name: Mylapore to R.A. Puram
reaches.verdict: Five MRTS crossings and three stations sit on or over the canal; about 5,000 houses stand on its banks.

facts.text: The MRTS was routed on the canal per a 1976-77 Planning Commission working group because no other corridor was economically available; the 2022 High Court order exempts its pillars from removal.

Around Mylapore roughly 5,000 houses stand on the canal banks; the 2023 restoration DPR for these reaches was set aside in Nov 2024 pending funds, and a fresh Rs 2,388 crore proposal to the Centre followed in Oct 2025.
facts.source: Citizen Matters / The News Minute; Hindusthan Samachar

facts.text: CAG found 17% of the canal's banks (16.5 of 96 km) encroached by 26,300 families, extended electricity, roads, water and ration cards.
facts.source: CAG Report No. 4 of 2017, Chapter IV

facts.text: Between 2015 and 2023, evictions from the city's waterway banks moved 19,817 families (about 79,000 people - roughly a third of two decades of such moves) largely to Kannagi Nagar, Ezhil Nagar and Perumbakkam: resettlement colonies built on the very marshland-floodplain this canal drains, which themselves flood.
facts.source: IRCDUC, 'Resettled in the Paths of Floods'

reaches.name: The Adyar crossing
reaches.verdict: In December 2015 the Adyar arrived here at nearly twice its own capacity and spilled through the canal into the neighbourhoods.

facts.text: The 2015 Adyar peak entering the city was ~3,800 cubic metres per second against a channel capacity of ~2,038.
Govindasamy Nagar, on PWD canal land here, was demolished from Apr 2022 after a 2011 Supreme Court ruling; families were dispersed to four resettlement sites.

reaches.name: Indira Nagar to Thiruvanmiyur
reaches.verdict: Eight MRTS crossings; the reach where the city's hyacinth-removal machines worked in 2021.

facts.text: In Sep 2021 the Chief Minister inspected pre-monsoon hyacinth removal with floating amphibian machines and robotic excavators on the canal near Indira Nagar MRTS station and Thiruvanmiyur Lattice Bridge.

reaches.name: Kottivakkam to the Okkiyam confluence
reaches.verdict: The most important junction on the canal: Okkiyam Maduvu, the Pallikaranai marsh's only drain, enters here - the reach where CMRL is widening the water opening under its crossing and where 2026 field reports tracked a construction-phase narrowing.

facts.text: Okkiyam Maduvu, a 2.8 km channel, is the sole outlet of the ~250 sq km Pallikaranai drainage (65 wetlands) into the canal, and the marsh's only brackish link to the sea at Muttukadu.
facts.source: TN State Wetlands Authority; Suzhal Arivom

facts.text: Metro Phase 2 viaduct works narrowed the channel under the OMR bridge from a pre-construction 83.73 m to under 10 m (field observations from 6 May 2026); a second narrowing sat at the Perumbakkam outlet; both sites fall inside the notified Ramsar boundary, within the crossing CMRL's widening programme serves.

Zero flamingo records anywhere in Pallikaranai from 1 Jan to 15 Jun 2026, attributed by the field report to the blocked tidal exchange; water hyacinth proliferated across both sides of the obstruction.

Our satellite screening independently shows this reach's corridor vegetation fraction jumping from 0.58 (Jan-Apr 2026) to 0.77 (Jun-Aug 2026), consistent with the documented hyacinth explosion; monsoon bank-greening also contributes, so ground-truth decides.
Modelling of the 2015 flood simulated a peak of 1,349.5 cubic metres per second (~47,700 cusecs) through Okkiyam Maduvu; the channel's stated capacity after post-Michaung works is 12,000 cusecs.

In 2015, absence of the dropped short-cut diversion channel forced 12,500 cusecs into a canal reach designed for 9,000, inundating Velachery and adjacent areas. The channel had been dropped in Oct 2014 after Rs 90.34 crore of a Rs 131.90 crore sanction was spent, over land acquisition costed at about Rs 100 crore.
In the current satellite window, 83% of this reach's mapped water surface reads as floating or emergent vegetation - the highest on the canal, against 2.5% at brackish Muttukadu.
facts.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis (NDVI over OSM water polygons)

reaches.name: Sholinganallur to Semmencheri
reaches.verdict: The widened reach, and the canal's one running success: 20 hectares of planted mangroves with better than 90% survival.

facts.text: The Forest Department's Green Tamil Nadu Mission planted 12,500 mangrove saplings across ~20 ha on the Muttukadu-Pallikaranai stretch in 2024 using a fishbone channel technique, with over 90% survival; 20,000 more seedlings followed in 2025-26.

CAG records the JNNURM improvement of this reach (to carry 9,000 cusecs) as completed in December 2014; a 2025 field check reported only ~2.5 km visibly widened to Injambakkam bridge; a field verification would reconcile the two records.
facts.source: CAG Report No. 4 of 2017 vs Uvakai Research Foundation field check

facts.text: Cement residue and construction debris were documented being dumped on the canal's outer embankments between Akkarai signal and Sholinganallur in June 2024, threatening South Chennai's primary flood outlet.
Median measured water width on this reach: 42 m - against 18 m in the MRTS reaches.

reaches.name: Uthandi to Muttukadu
reaches.verdict: A Rs 91 crore straight-cut to the sea is under construction here; the abandoned Muttukadu Boat House Lock closes the reach.

facts.text: The Uthandi straight-cut flood escape channel (Rs 91 crore, 550 cusecs capacity against the canal's 3,500) was tendered 8 Jul 2025 and began work in Aug 2025 amid CRZ objections and fisher protests; work has been suspended since Oct 2025 pending NGT proceedings. Water tests en route had found faecal coliform 1,600 MPN/100ml and BOD 26.5 mg/L.
The Muthukadu Boat House Lock, one of three abandoned navigation locks on the southern canal, stands at 12.8073 N 80.2414 E.

reaches.name: Muttukadu backwater and the Kovalam inlet
reaches.verdict: The canal's own flood mouth and its liveliest water: 126 bird species, a boat house, working fishers - and a sand bar that shuts it seven months a year.

facts.text: Muttukadu is a temporarily open/closed estuary: longshore drift closes the mouth roughly March-September; the monsoon reopens it; the mouth varies from a few metres to ~200 m. Water quality deteriorates sharply when closed, with recorded hypoxia fish kills.
126 bird species are on the live eBird list for Muttukadu Backwaters (captured 18 Aug 2026), corroborating the 2024 journal survey's 124 species (Jul 2021-Mar 2023 fieldwork, 7 near-threatened).
The brackish reaches read nearly vegetation-free in our satellite screening (0.09-0.12) while freshwater stagnant reaches choke - the salinity control on hyacinth, visible from orbit.
MAWS agreed Rs 1 crore to dredge and hold a 100 m opening at the mouth; TTDC (whose 1984 boat house anchors backwater tourism) sought WRD dredging.
Olive ridley nesting beaches run from the Adyar mouth south past Kovalam (Jan-Apr season); any works at this mouth sit beside an active nesting beach.

reaches.name: Kelambakkam south to Thaiyur
reaches.verdict: Backwater flats with flamingos and pelicans on one side, and the Kovalam-Nemmeli wetland - now proposed as a city reservoir - on the other.

facts.text: The Kovalam-Nemmeli 'Great Salt Lake' (~5,000 acres) is a hand-fishery and shorebird wetland fed twice daily by tides through the Muttukadu and Kokilamedu inlets; the canal carries catchment surplus through it.

The proposed Mamallan reservoir would convert the wetland for 170 MLD of city supply; the project EIA itself recorded 102 bird species, and 22 scientists wrote to the Chief Minister warning of irreversible damage.

7,000 Avicennia marina saplings were planted in Kovalam creek in 2022-23 after clearing invasive Prosopis, with Irula community help; 100 acres near the Kelambakkam toll plaza are identified for phase 2.

reaches.name: Manamai to Poonjeri
reaches.verdict: Eleven structure-free kilometres where the canal survives un-encroached: quiet, green with vegetation, and the easiest stretch of the alignment to restore.

facts.text: Our satellite screening shows this reach as a continuous vegetated channel with almost no open water at 10 m resolution (corridor vegetation 0.55-0.61, water near zero) - see the km 64-66 chip.
IWAI's survey found the southern canal's banks unprotected up to the Mahabalipuram Road Bridge, with depths of 0.3-1.3 m.

reaches.name: Mahabalipuram
reaches.verdict: The scope ends at Poonjeri, 1.5 km from the monuments, where IWAI once drew a terminal that was never built.

facts.text: IWAI's 2014 scheme placed a proposed Mahabalipuram terminal at 12.6169 N 80.1868 E; the Rs 123.40 crore Thiruvanmiyur-Kalpakkam development stalled with ~Rs 4 crore spent.
South of scope, the canal continues toward Kalpakkam, where the MAPS cooling-water return raises canal level up to 20 cm for 20 km.

chapters.title: A canal that carries everything except boats
chapters.verdict: Built 1806-1882 to carry salt, firewood and dried fish into Madras, the Buckingham Canal today is Chennai's flood carrier and the spine of the city's eastern waterways: 74.5 km, measured here end to end, fifty metres at a time.

chapters.title: The industrial mouth
chapters.verdict: Regulation has steadily moved industry's routine discharges off the canal; what remains to manage is the city's sewage and the storm-season event. Continuous measurement is how the next question gets answered in hours.

chapters.title: The city squeeze
chapters.verdict: Between the Cooum and the Adyar, survey records give the canal 42 to 143 metres; today's water measures 9.3 m at the narrowest. Restoration mathematics starts from the measured number, and this page carries it every 200 metres.

chapters.title: The marsh's only drain
chapters.verdict: Everything South Chennai drains passes through one 2.8 km channel into the canal. It is the system's most sensitive point: weather, works and weeds all register here first, which is why it rewards the closest watch.

chapters.title: The living estuary
chapters.verdict: Where the tide still reaches, the canal still lives: 126 bird species, working fishers, a boat house - behind a sand bar that closes seven months a year.

chapters.title: The intact ribbon
chapters.verdict: South of Kovalam the canal is quiet and un-encroached: eleven structure-free kilometres, running green with vegetation - the easiest stretch of the alignment to restore.

chapters.title: The investment runway
chapters.verdict: Since 2008 the canal has gathered a national-waterway designation, a High Court restoration mandate, audits and sanctions - and in 2026, the largest funding window in its history. The intent is aligned; this page is the baseline to build on.

chapters.title: The measurement layer
chapters.verdict: Rs 1,281.88 crore stands sanctioned across these waterways, an Urban Challenge Fund approval is reported at Rs 7,500 crore, and the Water Metro study is out to tender. Investment at that scale deserves knowledge that keeps pace with it. This page is the baseline of that knowledge; what follows is what a first year of measurement on the water would add.

timeline.label: Canal declared part of National Waterway 4
JNNURM macro-drainage sanction incl. canal widening and a short-cut diversion channel
Diversion channel discontinued after Rs 90.34 cr of works; IWAI's Rs 123.40 cr Thiruvanmiyur-Kalpakkam scheme launched (~Rs 4 cr of works recorded)
The December flood: 12,500 cusecs forced into a 9,000-cusec reach; Velachery inundated
CAG quantifies 242.73 MLD of raw sewage entering CMA water bodies incl. the canal (CMWSSB estimate, Apr 2019)

Umbrella sanction for the canal, its associated drains and the Adyar and Cooum major drains: G.O.(D) No.419, MAWS, 3 Dec 2020; Rs 408.08 crore of it for the canal (Ennore to Muttukadu, 48 km) and Rs 1,014.28 crore allocated to WRD for 35 works
timeline.source: Madras HC order in W.P. No. 6609 of 2014 (12 Sep 2022), para 14; NGT status report in O.A. 299 of 2013 (01.02.2024); WRD Policy Note 2025-26

timeline.label: KfW Kovalam-basin and ADB Kosasthalaiyar-basin drainage programmes (outfalls to the canal system)
Madras HC orders demarcation in 6 months, encroachment removal in 1 year, IWAI custody; MRTS pillars exempted; sewage mitigation plan ordered
WRD restoration DPR submitted (Anna University DGPS survey)

Of the 35 WRD works under the Rs 1,281.88 crore sanction, 30 commenced; after the December 2023 floods and the Advisory Committee on Flood Risk in Chennai Metro, the detailed project reports were taken up for review and the works held, with five works (Rs 160.73 crore) untendered pending resettlement; rehabilitation of four canals confluencing in the Buckingham Canal (Rs 120.44 crore) is in progress
Rs 60.79 crore of the comprehensive restoration works under the Rs 1,281.88 crore sanction moves from Chennai Rivers Restoration Trust funds to State funds

Uthandi straight-cut tendered (550 cusecs; Jul 2025; work suspended Oct 2025; NGT (SZ) suo motu order of 17 Sep 2025 directing agency affidavits, with CMWSSB's January 2026 report recording the sewage discharges); PWD proposes full-canal restoration to the Centre; Rs 31 cr Chepauk-Greenways starter with IWAI; water-metro feasibility begins
timeline.amount: Rs 91 cr + Rs 2,388 cr (proposal) + Rs 31 cr
timeline.source: Uvakai; Hindusthan Samachar; ProjectX India; NGT (SZ) suo motu proceedings on the straight-cut discharges

timeline.label: Urban Challenge Fund phase-1 in-principle approval for Cooum-Adyar-Buckingham restoration reported at Rs 7,500 crore (Times of India via Swarajya; no official project list published as of 20 Aug 2026); CMRL floats the Water Metro DFR-cum-DPR tender for Ennore-Mahabalipuram (NIT 13 Aug; bids close 18 Sep 2026)
timeline.source: Swarajya 11 Jun 2026 (citing Times of India); MoHUA UCF Operational Guidelines, Apr 2026; CMRL NIT TDR-76-WM/2026 dt 13 Aug 2026

silt_ledger.text: The last published depth survey of the southern canal found 0.3 to 1.3 m of water against a 1.8 m navigation target; no public bathymetry has been recorded since. A boat-run depth transect is the pilot's first field deliverable.
At the Ennore end, fly-ash silt about 1 m deep on a 2.5 km stretch is under a WRD dredging programme (~4.30 lakh cubic metres) running since mid-2020.
silt_ledger.source: The Hindu via ICSF; NGT record

silt_ledger.text: Ahead of Cyclone Michaung, reporting put the bed at 2 ft below mean sea level against a historical 6 ft - the working measure of accumulated silt in the city reaches.
GCC removed 16,270 tonnes of silt and water hyacinth from 44 canals and water bodies between 2 May and 10 July 2026 in monsoon preparation; per-canal splits are with the contracts.
The Oct 2025 restoration proposal prices dredging the full 167 km to 1.5-3.0 m depth at a uniform 40 m width - the clearest official statement of where depths stand today.

width_ledger.note: The Cooum-Adyar link, road by road. 'Recorded in the survey era' is the canal's width in the original survey records - the full recorded extent, banks included, so it reads as the canal's entitlement, not just open water. 'Found in ~2012' is what the HSCTC feasibility study measured on the ground; 'Measured 2026' is our transect measurement of today's water surface. In every column the two numbers are the minimum and maximum along that stretch. A dash means we would rather show nothing than an uncertain join.
width_ledger.source: HSCTC (Chennai High Speed Circular Transportation Corridors) feasibility report, c. 2012, via Wikipedia (table added 25 Aug 2013)
width_ledger.claim_text: Cooum-Adyar width ledger, 14 stretches: original survey vs HSCTC (~2012) widths
width_ledger.today_line: 2026 measurements: Neer Vazhvu transects at 50 m spacing from OpenStreetMap water polygons; across all these reaches the median is 18 m with a 6.5 m minimum.

channel: Fly-ash dredging of the creek complex is an active WRD programme (~4.30 lakh m3 scope since 2020).
interception: No canal-specific outfall is documented on this reach; the load arrives with the creek system.
constraints: TNPCB's fish-kill investigation (Aug 2026) is live; Kamarajar Port and TANGEDCO interfaces govern access.
NCSCM's Rs 45.99 crore creek eco-restoration (2023-25) is in progress under NGT OA 152/2023.
surveys: Flow-gauging site nomination at the creek junction

channel: Ash slurry pipeline crossings and reported dead-flow spots define the channel condition here.
The News Minute; India Water Portal
constraints: Power-station cooling circuits (consented into the creek) shape the hydraulics.

channel: CPCL's consented monsoon stormwater route enters here, with online sensors and booms as consent conditions.
constraints: Refinery-belt access and the Dec 2023 oil-spill legacy govern works planning.

interception: Three Kodungaiyur STP outlets (40+80+110 MLD) and six Tiruvottiyur pumping stations (>=7.25 MLD raw) are the documented inflows - the densest interception workload on the canal.
TNPCB CCWW 2022-23; Arappor Iyakkam RTI audit
constraints: Kodungaiyur dumpyard bank; the city's worst Culex clusters flank this reach.
programmes: ADB Kosasthalaiyar-basin drains (outfalls to this system)

interception: Otteri Nullah and the Captain Cotton Canal join at Basin Bridge - two of the city's largest drain loads arrive here.

channel: The city squeeze begins: rail infrastructure hems the channel past Central and the yards.
constraints: Rail-yard land interfaces (Southern Railway) govern any widening here.
programmes: CMWSSB outfall plugging across the city waterways: revised sanction Rs 385.38 crore, 36 works, 34 complete and 2 in progress (NGT status report 01.02.2024; MAWS Policy Note 2025-26)

channel: This is the tidal Cooum itself: works here belong to the Cooum restoration scope, not canal packages.
Bridge vents at Ice House Road and Kutchery Road were built 5-6 m against a required 15-17 m and were never widened (CAG); vent widening is a named, unfinished work item.
Width recovery envelope: recorded 42-143 m on this link, measured median 18 m today (the width ledger carries the road-by-road detail).
interception: The sewage mitigation plan ordered by the High Court (2022) applies with full force here - the Wallajah Road monitoring station records the load.
constraints: MRTS pillars are exempt from the HC removal order; demarcation stalled in the central constituencies.
programmes: Rs 31 cr Chepauk-Greenways initial restoration (this reach)

channel: The Central-canal flood-wall programme collapsed from 14,200 m to 1,115 m over eviction constraints (Rs 68.62 cr sanction, Rs 15.72 cr spent) - the remaining wall length is a known, unfinished quantity.
interception: Unauthorised sewer connections from bank settlements are the documented local load.
constraints: About 5,000 houses stand on the banks; the 2023 DPR for these reaches was set aside in Nov 2024 pending funds, with a successor proposal filed Oct 2025.
programmes: Rs 31 cr Chepauk-Greenways initial restoration (this reach)

constraints: The Adyar estuary junction: works here interact with Adyar-mouth dredging and the eco-park reach.

channel: Eight MRTS crossings set the narrowing pattern; hyacinth-removal machinery has worked this reach (2021 CM inspection).
CMRL's programme to widen the water opening at the Okkiyam crossing (widened to 200 m, clearance raised, bed desilted toward a 12,000-cusec capacity) is the active works precedent on the canal.
interception: Perungudi-side STP discharges (54+60 MLD plus Alandur and Sholinganallur) arrive via the Pallikaranai system.
constraints: Okkiyam Maduvu falls inside the Pallikaranai Ramsar boundary; CMDA froze planning permissions in the 1 km zone (Office Order 07/2025). Evidence-first is the only lawful entry.

channel: CAG records the 9,000-cusec improvement completed Dec 2014; a 2025 field check saw ~2.5 km visibly widened - an as-built verification survey would reconcile the records.
interception: Sholinganallur STP (18 MLD) discharges on this system.
constraints: The 20 ha mangrove plantation (>90% survival) is a live restoration asset any works must design around - and can extend (fishbone technique, ~200 ha potential).
surveys: As-built verification vs the JNNURM record
programmes: Green Tamil Nadu Mission mangroves (this reach)

channel: The Rs 91 cr Uthandi straight-cut (550 cusecs) was tendered Jul 2025 and began from this reach; work has been suspended since Oct 2025 pending NGT proceedings. The abandoned Muttukadu Boat House Lock anchors the south end.
constraints: CRZ objections and fisher protests accompanied the straight-cut's start - stakeholder interface is live.

channel: Mouth management is budgeted (MAWS Rs 1 cr to dredge and hold a 100 m opening); IWAI's 2014 scheme priced lock rebuilds at Muttukadu and Kovalam South.
interception: NGT filings admit sewage discharges reaching the estuary; tanker dumping was caught here.
CMWSSB report to NGT; Citizen Matters
constraints: Olive ridley nesting beaches adjoin the mouth (Jan-Apr season); TTDC tourism and CIBA's research station operate on the backwater.
surveys: Bathymetry of the backwater (last envelope: <=2 m, 2018 study)

channel: Kovalam creek mangrove restoration has a identified phase-2 site (100 acres near Kelambakkam toll).
constraints: The proposed Mamallan reservoir would convert the adjoining Kovalam-Nemmeli wetland; 22 scientists have written to the CM - scope interacts with a live policy question.
surveys: Bathymetry (no public survey exists for Kelambakkam backwater)

channel: Eleven structure-free kilometres with un-encroached banks (IWAI records them unprotected): the largest uninterrupted stretch for works on the alignment; the channel currently runs vegetation-choked.
IWAI's 2014 scheme placed a terminal here (never built); the canal continues south toward Kalpakkam.
constraints: The Mamallapuram monuments zone (~1.5 km east) brings heritage-authority interfaces.

methods.title: Length and chainage
methods.body: The 74.5 km alignment is chained from OpenStreetMap's canal geometry (ODbL, snapshot August 2026), km 0 at the Ennore creek crossing, resampled every 50 m. OSM has no continuous canal through the Basin Bridge / Cooum junction; a roughly 1.4 km straight bridge spans it, so chainage there is approximate. Whole-length uncertainty: about plus or minus 1-2%.

methods.title: Widths (the 1,492 transects)
methods.body: Every 50 m of chainage we cast a perpendicular line and measure the water-surface polygon traced by OpenStreetMap contributors (edits 2018 to 2026, most since 2022). 1,012 transects return a measurement. 50 m sampling sits close to the resolution of the source itself: the traced bank lines place a vertex every 36 m at the median, so sampling much finer would only re-read straight drawn edges. Width is water surface at the tracing moment, not the canal's recorded land, and it moves with season. Individual transects: treat as plus or minus 15-25% on narrow reaches; per-reach medians are robust. Each reach carries a confidence tier: A = at least 70% measured, tracing mostly 2021 or later, and width jitter at 200 m separation of 25% or less; B = measured but sparse or older tracing; C = not channel-measurable (creek complexes, junctions). Jitter is always evaluated at about 200 m separation, whatever the sampling density, so denser sampling cannot inflate a tier. Wide spreads on reaches that open into backwaters are real variation, not error.

methods.title: Satellite metrics (Sentinel-2, 10 m pixels)
methods.body: Cloud-masked median composites: January-April and June-August 2026. Vegetation = NDVI above 0.35; open water = NDWI above 0. Vegetation on the water is computed strictly inside the mapped water polygons (floating plus emergent growth); corridor figures also include about 8 m of bank each side and read higher. The condition strip reads a 25 m disc every 50 m of chainage; with 10 m pixels, 50 m is the honest floor for this. Threshold choice moves fractions by roughly 5-10 percentage points; 10 m pixels undercount water in channels narrower than about 30 m. The suspended-sediment reading (NDTI) is a relative index over open water, not a mg/L measurement. Site images are clearest-pixel composites; segment images are medians; each is dated on the image.

methods.title: The built edge
methods.body: Google Open Buildings v3 footprints (2023 release, confidence at least 0.7) counted within 50 m and 100 m of the centerline. Deliberately conservative: measured from the centerline, not the canal's recorded boundary; the confidence filter trims small structures; three years of construction post-date the data. A 'none mapped' reads exactly that: nothing in the dataset, not proof of nothing on the ground.

methods.title: Check the numbers yourself
methods.body: Every input is public: OpenStreetMap (ODbL, snapshot date stated), Copernicus Sentinel-2, Google Open Buildings, and the cited government documents - many held as local primary copies (IWAI 2014, CAG 2017 and 2020, the Madras HC order, the WRD and MAWS Policy Notes, TNPCB consent orders, CPCB monitoring PDFs). Every derived number on this page is recomputed independently from the raw inputs before publication by a published audit script (scripts/audit_waterway_numbers.py in the Neer Vazhvu repository), and the claim register (claims.json) carries a per-number citation a reader can pull and compare.

methods.title: What this page deliberately does not compute
methods.body: Depth, silt volume and flow: no satellite can measure them in water this turbid and narrow (the last public depth survey is from 2014), and we would rather show a gap than an estimate without an instrument. They are the first work of the measurement layer this page proposes: level and flow gauging to the index-velocity standard, a boat-run depth survey, and field checks under the vegetation the satellite flags.
